label: delimiter step when the first token to recall is h/0/f (plus weak w at t=0)
explanation: About 87% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step, but it fires on only about 8% of delimiters. Which delimiters it fires on depends on the tokens about to be recalled: it is strongest when orig(0) is h (12x lift), 0 or f, and weaker when it is 1 or y. orig(1) also contributes (next_out 0/h/1/f/y), and a small spillover onto the first copy step (recall_idx 1) happens when out_tok is h. Longer sequences (L 8-9) carry more of the mass. A second, separate low-magnitude mode is input w at t=0, which accounts for many activations but only about 3% of the mass. It does not fire in the later copy phase (recall_idx >= 2) or in the original phase after t=0. The behavior looks like a graded weighted sum over the upcoming tokens rather than a clean category, so delimiters starting with f/0 are often below threshold (about 5k false positives), and delimiters where only orig(1) is h/0/1/y are missed.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=0 & in_tok=w (+10.70), t=1 & prev_tok=o (+6.15), out_tok=h (+4.25), in_tok=w (+4.10), out_tok=f (+4.08), out_tok=0 (+3.93). Lower it: phase=2 (-8.44), next_out=w (-3.61), next_out=k (-3.58), in_tok=0 (-3.48).
